context: Thread has_header from the benchmark's csv_has_header attribute (resolved next to the existing csv_delimiter) through _convert_table_files into convert_csv_to_parquet, and set ReadOptions(skip_rows=1) when a header is declared AND explicit column names are supplied. Gate the pass-through on format_type == 'csv' so .tbl stays headerless regardless of the attribute. Bump DATAFRAME_CACHE_VERSION so stale caches built from the broken path are not reused.
description: FormatConverter.convert_csv_to_parquet passes the schema's column names to pyarrow.csv.ReadOptions(column_names=...). That REPLACES the header names but does NOT skip the header LINE, so a headered CSV is parsed with its own header as the first data row. With declared numeric/date column types the conversion then FAILS ('CSV conversion error to int64: invalid value day_of_week'), and _convert_table_files logs 'Failed to convert <table>, using source file' and falls back to the RAW CSV -- an untyped read where date columns stay strings. Every downstream date filter then matches nothing, so the DataFrame surface silently returns zero rows instead of erroring. Headerless TPC .tbl is unaffected (it has no header), which is why this survived: every gated benchmark so far is .tbl or headerless. Found by wiring a FlightData cross-surface gate, whose CSVs carry headers -- all 20 queries x 2 backends diverged. The benchmark already declares csv_has_header=True; the converter simply never received it.

preserves.behavior: Declared column types still apply; the fix must not reintroduce PyArrow type inference
Headerless sources (TPC .tbl, headerless CSV) keep every row -- no off-by-one from skipping a line that is not a header
